[[Category:Special function]]
The '''logit function''' is a strictly increasing, real-valued [[function]].

It is the inverse of the [[sigmoid function]].

== Definition ==

$$
\operatorname{logit}:(0,1)\to\mathbb{R}\\
\operatorname{logit}(p)=\ln\left(\frac{p}{1-p}\right).
$$

== Properties ==

=== Limits ===

The logit is strictly increasing, with limits

$$
\lim_{p\to0^+}\operatorname{logit}(p)=-\infty,
\qquad
\lim_{p\to1^-}\operatorname{logit}(p)=+\infty.
$$

=== Symmetry ===

$$
\operatorname{logit}(1-p)=-\operatorname{logit}(p).
$$

=== Derivative ===

$$
\dot{\operatorname{logit}}(p)=\frac{1}{p(1-p)}.
$$
